notes.title: -(으)ㄹ 만하다
notes.text: -(으)ㄹ 만하다 means "worth doing" or "decent enough": 볼 만해요 (worth seeing), 먹을 만해요 (worth eating), 참을 만해요 (bearable). It's every reviewer's favorite phrase: 이 영화 볼 만해요! Gangneung is famous for its squid and its clear East Sea.

notes.title: Crossing the street
notes.text: 횡단보도 = crosswalk, 신호등 = traffic light, 빨간불 / 초록불 = red / green light. Korean walk signals count down the seconds. 네거리 (or 사거리) is a four-way intersection; 큰길 is the main road.

notes.title: -았/었던
notes.text: -았/었던 + noun points to something that happened and is now over: 자주 갔던 카페 (the café I used to go to — but don't anymore), 처음 만났던 날 (the day we first met). Compare -던 (habit, unfinished): 다니던 학교 (the school I was attending). An old neighborhood 목욕탕 (bathhouse) is a slice of classic Korean life.

notes.title: -더라고요
notes.text: -더라고요 shares something you personally saw or experienced, often with a touch of surprise: 바다가 정말 맑더라고요 (The sea was so clear — I saw it). 그 아가씨, 울더라고요 (She was crying, I noticed). Use it for things you observed, not for your own feelings.

lessons.goal: Talk about the journey back to the big city.

scene.ko: 서울로 돌아가는 기차가 터널을 지나가요.
scene.en: The train back to Seoul passes through a tunnel.
b: to pass by, to go through

scene.ko: 별 씨 곁에 거의 갔는데…
scene.en: We were so close to Byeol…

scene.ko: 괜찮아. 첫눈이 오면 온다고 했잖아. 우리 앞길은 밝아.
scene.en: It's OK. She said she'll come with the first snow. There's good news ahead for us.
b: to be okay, to be fine
the first snow of the year

scene.ko: 그런데 별 씨 걸음이 정말 빠르더라.
scene.en: But Byeol walks fast, I noticed.

scene.ko: 서울역. 대도시의 길거리는 사람들로 가득해요. 사람들이 바쁘게 오가요.
scene.en: Seoul Station. The big-city streets are packed with people hurrying back and forth.

scene.ko: 지하도로 가요! 전철 사 호선을 타요.
scene.en: Let's go through the underpass! We take subway Line 4.

scene.ko: 지우야, 뛰어나가지 마! 길 잃어버려!
scene.en: Ji-woo, don't run off! You'll get lost!
b: to stop, to not do (-지 마세요)
to throw away; (-아 버리다 = end up doing)

scene.ko: 할머니가 마중 나오셨어요! 할머니!
scene.en: Grandma came to meet us! Grandma!

scene.ko: 할머니도 웃으면서 뛰어와요.
scene.en: Grandma comes hurrying over too, smiling.

scene.ko: 하숙집 뒷산 너머로 달이 떴어요. 긴 여행이 끝났어요.
scene.en: The moon has risen over the hill behind the boarding house. The long trip is over.

notes.title: The subway
notes.text: Seoul's subway (지하철, also called 전철) has numbered lines — 일 호선, 이 호선… — plus named ones. Signs are in Korean, English, Chinese and Japanese, and every station has a number. A 지하도 is an underground walkway; many lead straight into the subway.
